title: What If All the Dark Matter in the Universe Vanished?

scenes.text: What if dark matter vanished tonight? You would never see it happen, but galaxies would.
Dark matter is about 27 percent of the universe. Ordinary matter, everything we can touch, is only about 5.
In the 1970s, Vera Rubin found stars at galaxy edges moving fast enough to escape.
Without the extra gravity, those stars would fly off into empty space.
Galaxy clusters, moving too fast to stay together, would unravel too.
And in the early universe, simulations say galaxies might never have formed at all, so there would be no us.

description:
What if all dark matter vanished?
Galaxies would lose the invisible glue that holds their stars in place.
What should we run through next?
